plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in late winter, long celebrated in East Asian art and poetry for blooming despite cold and occasional snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are among the first flowers of the year in Japan, and ume festivals are held across the country in February, often weeks before cherry blossom season.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes up through frost and snow in woodlands and gardens.
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce a compound called galantamine, which is used in medication for symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Hamamelis x intermedia
plants.description: A large deciduous shrub with spidery, ribbon-like petals that curl up in cold weather and unfurl in milder spells. The flowers have a spicy, sweet fragrance and appear on leafless branches.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Hybrid garden origin; cultivated in temperate regions of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Witch hazel's petals curl up tightly to protect themselves during freezing temperatures and then expand again when it warms.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall tropical and subtropical tree with feathery fern-like foliage that bears dense clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In some regions, bloom can occur in late summer when conditions are warm.
plants.bloomingSeason: Variable; some trees flower in late summer in the Southern Hemisphere (February to March) and others in spring (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: Fallen jacaranda blossoms carpet streets in purple, and in Pretoria, South Africa, the trees are so abundant that it is nicknamed the Jacaranda City.
